t: A sultanate on the Blue Nile, ruled from Sennar from 1504 to 1821, that took the place of the Christian Nubian kingdom of Alodia.
Its wealth came from gold, ivory and slaves traded to Egypt and the Red Sea, and its sultans ruled through vassal lords such as the Abdallab.
Under Funj rule Islam and Arabic spread across the middle Nile through Sufi orders and holy men, shaping modern Sudanese identity.
dyk: The Scottish traveller James Bruce passed through Sennar in 1772 on his way back from Ethiopia and left one of the few eyewitness accounts of the Funj court.
ev: Amara Dunqas founds Sennar, according to tradition
Funj and Abdallab forces destroy Soba, capital of Christian Alodia
Sultan Adlan I defeats and kills the Abdallab ruler Ajib at Karkoj
Reign of Badi II Abu Diqn, who builds a slave army
Funj forces defeat the Ethiopian emperor Iyasu II on the Dinder River
Hamaj regents take power after deposing Badi IV
Badi VII submits to the Egyptian army of Ismail Kamil Pasha
